title: Erdős #897 OQ-01 (Part I): Non-Vacuity, Selectivity, and a Strongly-Additive Reduction

problemStatement.formal: Let $f$ be additive with $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k)/\log(p^k) = \infty$. **Part I (OPEN)**: must $\limsup_n (f(n+1)-f(n))/\log n = \infty$? This entry does not assert Part I. It proves the verified scaffolding: (1) the hypothesis is satisfiable (an explicit additive, indeed strongly additive, witness); (2) the classical examples $\log$ and $\omega$ fail the hypothesis; (3) the hypothesis forces $f$ unbounded above on prime powers; (4) for strongly additive $f$ the hypothesis reduces to $f(p)/\log p$ unbounded over primes.
problemStatement.plain: Verified, axiom-free surrounding theory for Part I of Erdős #897 (OPEN): if an additive f grows faster than log on prime powers (limsup f(p^k)/log(p^k) = ∞), must (f(n+1)-f(n))/log n also be unbounded? The forward implication is open and is NOT asserted. Instead this entry establishes the theory any analysis of Part I needs. (1) Non-vacuity: an explicit additive witness logSqWeight(n) = ∑_{p|n} (log p)² satisfies the hypothesis, so Part I is not vacuously true — and the witness is even strongly additive. (2) Selectivity: the parent file's flagship functions log and ω both FAIL the hypothesis (log sits at the boundary, ω is bounded on prime powers), so the hypothesis is a strict growth condition. (3) The hypothesis forces plain unboundedness of f on prime powers. (4) A strongly-additive reduction collapsing the hypothesis to a condition on the primes alone, mirroring the parent's completely-additive reduction. Verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

proven: exists_additive_unboundedOnPrimePowers: the headline non-vacuity result — there is an additive function satisfying UnboundedOnPrimePowers, so Part I of Erdős #897 is not vacuously true. Witness: logSqWeight(n) = ∑_{p|n} (log p)².

logSqWeight_additive / logSqWeight_stronglyAdditive: the witness is additive (disjoint prime supports of coprime numbers split the sum) and in fact strongly additive (logSqWeight(p^k) = logSqWeight(p) = (log p)²), so it is governed by the strongly-additive reduction below.

not_unboundedOnPrimePowers_logN and not_unboundedOnPrimePowers_omega: selectivity of the hypothesis — the parent file's flagship additive functions log and ω both FAIL it. log sits exactly at the boundary (log(p^k)/log(p^k) = 1) and ω is bounded on prime powers (ω(p^k) = 1). The hypothesis therefore isolates functions growing strictly faster than log on prime powers.

unboundedOnPrimePowers_unbounded: the hypothesis forces plain unboundedness — for every B some prime power has f(p^k) > B, obtained by dialing the defining constant M against the uniform lower bound log(p^k) ≥ log 2.

stronglyAdditive_unboundedOnPrimePowers_iff: a strongly-additive reduction collapsing UnboundedOnPrimePowers f to 'f(p)/log p unbounded over primes', the strongly-additive counterpart of the parent file's completely-additive reduction. The cancellation is different: the value is constant in k, so the binding case is k = 1, and the M < 0 branch is handled by invoking the hypothesis at 0.

not_unboundedOnPrimePowers_of_bounded (Section 10) — boundedness selectivity criterion: any function bounded above by a constant C on prime powers (f(p^k) ≤ C) fails the #897 hypothesis, since C is dominated by (max(C,0)/log2)·log(p^k) (log(p^k) ≥ log2 > 0), reducing to the O(log) criterion of section (8). Generalizes ω selectivity to any prime-power-bounded function.
insights: **Non-vacuity matters for open problems**: without an explicit witness, Part I could be vacuously true. logSqWeight certifies the hypothesis is genuinely satisfiable — and by a strongly additive function, the most structured class.

**The hypothesis is a strict growth condition**: log is the boundary (ratio identically 1) and ω is bounded on prime powers, so both flagship examples fail. The hypothesis selects functions growing strictly faster than log on prime powers.

**Constant-in-k is the key to the strongly-additive reduction**: unlike the completely-additive case where k cancels in a ratio, here the value does not depend on k, so the worst case is simply k = 1.
**Squaring the log is the cheapest super-log weight**: (log p)²/log p = log p → ∞ gives the required divergence with a one-line estimate, avoiding any heavier construction.

The merged Erdos897OQ01.lean had silently drifted out of buildability against current pinned Mathlib (unboundedOnPrimePowers_smul, lines 190/194): field_simp now closes the goal making a trailing ring error 'No goals', and (mul_lt_mul_left hc).mpr fails to synthesize. Confirmed genuine (not infra) by building the pristine origin/main file after a full --repair-cache. Version-stable replacements: mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left and dropping the redundant ring.

The hypothesis class UnboundedOnPrimePowers is an UP-SET in the prime-power domination order: unboundedOnPrimePowers_of_ge (largeness transfers upward) and its exact contrapositive not_unboundedOnPrimePowers_of_le (failure transfers downward) are the two halves. The concrete lower boundary is O(log): f(p^k) <= C*log(p^k) for a fixed C => fails, for every C. This single criterion unifies the ad-hoc selectivity of logN (C=1) and omega (C=1/log2) — both were proving instances of the same O(log) phenomenon.
